title: Emit schema-v1 audit events for private install/upgrade/rollback (operator + cluster metadata)
author: Bruno Silva
body:
Context
We need consistent audit coverage for Private deployment lifecycle actions (install/upgrade/rollback) as part of the audit logging program. This PR adds schema-v1 audit event emission to the private installer so enterprise customers can attribute cluster changes to a specific operator and correlate actions across the control plane.

What this changes
- Adds an audit emitter to the installer CLI that produces canonical schema-v1 events for:
  - private.install.started / private.install.completed / private.install.failed
  - private.upgrade.started / private.upgrade.completed / private.upgrade.failed
  - private.rollback.started / private.rollback.completed / private.rollback.failed
- Captures operator identity (actor) and cluster metadata (target) with explicit, non-secret fields.
- Introduces a small internal registry + JSONSchema validation step (fail-fast in tests, warn-and-continue at runtime) to prevent drift.

Event payload details (schema v1)
- event_schema: redwood.audit.v1
- event_version: 1
- event_name: private.(install|upgrade|rollback).(started|completed|failed)
- actor:
  - actor.type: user
  - actor.id: derived from --operator-id when provided; else a stable hash of --operator-email (never emits raw email)
  - actor.display: --operator-name (optional)
  - actor.source: "installer"
- target:
  - target.type: private_cluster
  - target.id: cluster_id (required) from --cluster-id (validated UUID-ish) or from the existing installer cluster-id file if present
  - target.attributes: { cluster_name (optional), k8s_namespace, region (optional), deployment_mode: "private" }
- request:
  - request_id: generated per command execution and threaded through all sub-steps
  - correlation_id: propagated from --correlation-id when invoked by automation
- context:
  - installer_version, package_version, package_digest (sha256), command, flags (allowlisted), git_sha (build-time), os/arch
- outcome:
  - outcome: success|failure
  - error_code: installer.<category>.<reason> (e.g., installer.k8s.apply_failed)
  - error_message: truncated and scrubbed (see redaction rules below)

Operator identity UX
- New required flag for lifecycle commands: --operator-id OR --operator-email
  - Rationale: relying on $USER / local machine identity is not sufficient for enterprise audit trails.
  - The installer will refuse to run without an operator identity unless --allow-missing-operator is explicitly set (intended for dev/testing only; prints a prominent warning and emits actor.type=unknown).
- Optional: --operator-name to show a human-friendly display name in downstream views.

Audit sink behavior
- If AUDIT_SINK_ENDPOINT is set (or --audit-endpoint), the installer POSTs events to the in-cluster audit-collector service (default: http://redwood-audit-collector.redwood-system.svc:8787/v1/audit/events).
- If no endpoint is configured, the installer writes JSONL events to: <install-root>/logs/audit-events.jsonl (to support air-gapped and "bring your own exporter" setups).
- Fail-open semantics: audit emission failure does NOT block install/upgrade/rollback by default. We log a structured warning and include the audit delivery error in the command summary.
  - New flag: --require-audit-delivery (enterprise hardening) to fail the command if the event cannot be delivered to the configured sink.

Redaction / safety
- Never emits kubeconfig contents, service account tokens, registry credentials, or any installer secrets.
- K8s API server URL is not logged; we only record a short hash (k8s_apiserver_fingerprint) for correlation without leaking internal endpoints.
- Error messages are scrubbed for common secret patterns ("token=", "Authorization:", "password", "secret") and truncated to 512 chars.

Files / areas changed (high level)
- cmd/installer/root.go: wire operator flags + request_id generation
- pkg/audit/emitter.go: sink interface (http + jsonl), retry policy for http
- pkg/audit/events.go: strongly-typed event builders per action/status
- pkg/audit/schema_v1.json: vendored schema snapshot + validation helper
- pkg/operations/install.go, upgrade.go, rollback.go: emit started/completed/failed around existing workflows
- pkg/cluster/metadata.go: cluster_id/namespace collection, apiserver fingerprinting
- docs/audit-logging.md: operator flag requirements + examples

Testing
- Unit tests for event builders (required fields present, redaction, stable actor hash behavior)
- Golden tests for JSON output (started/completed/failed variants)
- E2E (CI): dry-run install/upgrade emits JSONL with expected event_name + request_id

Rollout notes
- This is gated in production docs for enterprise enablement; we can default --require-audit-delivery on later once the in-cluster audit-collector is generally available.

Follow-ups
- Add explicit coverage for "uninstall" once that flow is finalized (tracked separately).
- Hook installer request_id to control plane rollout request_id when running under automation.

References
- Linear: ENG-2487
- Program: Audit log schema standardization + sensitive action coverage
commits: feat(audit): add audit emitter interface + http/jsonl sinks
feat(installer): require operator identity flags for lifecycle commands
feat(private): emit audit events for install/upgrade/rollback started/completed/failed
test(audit): golden tests for schema v1 event payloads + redaction
docs: add private installer audit logging usage
conversation:
Marcus Lin (review): We should not accept $USER as a default operator; enterprise auditors will ask how identity is verified. Can we make operator identity required and force an explicit override in dev?
Bruno Silva (author): Agree. Updated to require --operator-id or --operator-email. Added --allow-missing-operator for dev only (prints warning + actor.type=unknown). Tests updated.

Nadia Rahman (review): How are we ensuring schema drift doesn’t sneak in? Also please avoid logging kube API server URL.
Bruno Silva (author): Added vendored schema_v1.json + validator. Builders are typed + golden tests. For apiserver URL: now only logs a fingerprint hash (sha256 truncated) and never the URL.

Colin O'Donnell (review): For air-gapped installs, HTTP sink won’t exist. We need a deterministic local path for JSONL output. Also confirm we don’t fail the install if audit write fails.
Bruno Silva (author): Implemented jsonl sink at <install-root>/logs/audit-events.jsonl when no endpoint configured. Default is fail-open; added --require-audit-delivery for customers who want hard enforcement.

Olga Petrov (review): Please ensure error_message truncation is explicit and that we have a stable identifier for the cluster (cluster_id). Auditors hate mutable names.
Bruno Silva (author): error_message truncates at 512 chars and runs through scrubber. cluster_id is required (validated); cluster_name is optional.

Amina Yusuf (review): Minor: please add an example invocation in docs showing operator flags + correlation-id.
Bruno Silva (author): Done (docs/audit-logging.md). Added example for automation.

release_notes:
- Private installer now emits schema-v1 audit events for install/upgrade/rollback, including operator identity and cluster metadata.
- Adds JSONL fallback for air-gapped environments and optional --require-audit-delivery for strict enforcement.
- Introduces redaction and truncation for error payloads to avoid leaking secrets.
